Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are Ouija boards really dangerous in a way that a demonic entity can be let in?
Old_Answer: Yes. The imagination is one of the most important, potent, creative faculties at mankind’s disposal. The use of speculation, when it comes to matters involving the future, whether it is in “sports” like gambling on the horses or the slot machine, or using a “magic” board to let you in on secrets makes the human mind search for the unknown and to some extent unknowable (except through God) IN the unknown… It’s like going to a ballot box and voting on Door Number 1 without knowing what is behind door number 1. This kind of non-thinking, yet pining for some sort of “significant” or meaningful result raises the fear or anxiety level in a person, which also makes one prone to grasp any straw that volunteers itself. If the good can come through this way (and it doesn’t, for the good is not imprecise nor wishy washy nor speculative per se), then so can the bad. Therefore, stay away from these things. It is your desire to have something for free (as opposed to seeking counsel from God with whom you are in a relationship) that allows the dark side to bind you. You are volunteering for the bondage. Why go slave when you can be a free man?
Answer_with_writing_sample: Thank you for posing this intriguing question about Ouija boards and the potential risks involved. Personally, I tread lightly when it comes to phenomena that engage the spiritual realm, as there is a lot we do not understand. The fascination with Ouija boards often stems from cultural narratives about the supernatural, leading many to believe that using one could inadvertently invite a demonic entity into one's life. While I’m neither an expert in the occult nor a theologian, I do think there’s valid caution to consider. First and foremost, a Ouija board is merely a tool, akin to a telephone; it’s what we choose to dial into that matters. If one approaches it with an open heart and mind, and perhaps some skepticism, they might be less likely to encounter anything malevolent. However, those who engage in such practices with fear or desperation may inadvertently attract negative energies. Furthermore, it’s worth noting that many individuals report feelings of unease following their use of Ouija boards, which can stem from psychological factors rather than any actual supernatural implications. Ultimately, if you feel uncomfortable or uneasy about the potential for danger, it’s best to err on the side of caution and avoid engaging with the board altogether. Trust your instincts—if something feels off, it likely is. Remember that safety, both mental and spiritual, should take precedence. Stay grounded and remember that engaging with the unknown can be as perilous as it is fascinating.
Answer_with_user_profile: As a writer who enjoys exploring the intersection of psychology and spirituality, I find the topic of Ouija boards both fascinating and complex. Many people believe that using an Ouija board can open doors to the supernatural, potentially inviting negative entities or even demonic forces into one’s life. It’s important to understand that much of this belief stems from cultural narratives and personal experiences rather than solid evidence. The psychological aspect plays a significant role here; the ideomotor effect can lead participants to unconsciously move the planchette, creating an illusion of communication with spirits. This can instigate fear and anxiety, particularly if users approach the session with trepidation or preconceived notions of danger. Furthermore, the thrill of the unknown can amplify fear, making it seem like something sinister has occurred when, often, it’s simply a manifestation of our own subconscious. While there are certainly accounts of unsettling experiences, they can often be attributed to psychological factors rather than actual demonic interference. It’s essential to approach the use of an Ouija board with respect and caution, just like any tool involving the psyche. If one feels uncomfortable or fearful, it’s wise to avoid it altogether. Ultimately, whether Ouija boards are “dangerous” can depend largely on one’s mindset and intentions, so fostering a grounded and informed perspective is crucial when engaging with such practices.
Answer_with_full_information: Thank you for this thought-provoking question. The subject of Ouija boards often stirs a mix of intrigue, skepticism, and fear, and rightly so. Regardless of personal beliefs, it’s crucial to approach this topic with an open mind and a healthy dose of caution. Ouija boards have historically been associated with the spiritual and the unknown, and many who have dabbled with them report unsettling experiences. While some may argue that the board itself is merely a tool, the energy and intention one brings to it can significantly influence the outcome. It's said that an open mind can invite unexpected energies or entities, leading to experiences perceived as threatening or disturbing. This is not to say that a demonic entity is guaranteed to make an appearance; rather, individuals may inadvertently open themselves to influences they cannot control or understand. For some, the process can feel like an invitation into a realm that is best left unexplored. If you do choose to engage with one, I would strongly advise taking precautions: set clear intentions, maintain a grounded mindset, and preferably close the session properly. It’s essential to respect the power of the unknown, and whether or not you believe in spirits, the psychological impact of such experiences can be very real. In essence, while Ouija boards may not be inherently dangerous, the potential for unintended consequences is certainly worth considering. Tread carefully; it’s a delicate balance between curiosity and caution that should guide your exploration into such matters.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the one thing you feel you need to have to be truly content with your life, and what all would you sacrifice to get it?
Old_Answer: Number one thing: Reparations to all I have done wrong to or harmed, financially or otherwise. Especially, to my son, now an adult, whom I wronged through mistreatment. What all would I sacrifice to get it? First, my limited mindset about how best to produce financially has to go. Heretofore, I have operated out of only one framework: Start at the bottom, work hard, and rely on others to advance you. I need a better strategy. Presently, my son (and roommate) brings in more income than I; he is putting more money out for our overhead. It is reasonable, therefore, to be experiencing pressure to do better, both from within, and from without. Old habits die hard. They must be replaced by new ones with more payoffs. The biggest temptation is to hurry up and end the pain of cognitive dissonance, to get back up on that horse again, to once again join the majority of America’s lower-wage earners in a job with no benefits, where you don’t even know your schedule or number of hours from week to week, let alone are enabled to participate in a health insurance network that is worth your heard earned dough. But at least I’d be “doing my best,” right? “Doing right,” by “carrying my fair share,” isn’t that right? WRONG. All I would be doing is all that I have ever done before and it has NEVER worked. It ISN’T realistic that such an approach would ever work; it is an approach that has only functioned to bind me, to keep me down. You sit there in those positions, doing your best, all the while stilling your anger and discontent and reality-based worry about your future, thinking, “I’m doing the right thing;” Consoling yourself, “What else can be done?” Repeating mantras like, “It isn’t all my fault, that’s just the way things are.” Or worst of all, “Don’t worry, it’ll all be over soon.” I cannot and will not do that crap ever again in my life, period. So…. NEW STORY!! I’m flying off, like a straight-edged tangent, bouncing off that circle of enclosure over options that will never open to a different reality, earnestly applying myself instead to simple things, in order to change what has been the status quo in my life for years. I am shutting down what has been my modus operandi and risking being exposed for a phony, an ignoramus, an under-achiever who’s actually just stupid, or dumb, or whatever I think I might “really” be. Simple things first: I am treating my son with more kindness; finding ways to negotiate and stand up for myself with less scream and more “you and me,” not just me; focusing on progress and insisting I make some; making sure there’s something in it for him. In so doing, I am protecting that part of me that conceives; the heart/spirit/brain-womb in me, that captures reality potential floating through the air, that cannot lite upon the dry hard pan ground of sheer drudgery. Instead, I am refusing to off that fertile body’s offspring before it gets a chance to grow. I am protecting it, and in so doing, I am protecting me. Interestingly enough, it seems that baby ideas, like little babies in the human womb, only survive in safety, with something to hang onto. It’s not enough that an idea is good. Or, perhaps in respect of one of America’s biggest over achievers, Jeff Bezos, I can agree that inspiration is 1%, 99% of success is in execution. The support of branches, of a sturdy vine, a labyrinth of options to shelter that baby from what would strike it down, is what comes next. Therefore, besides setting aside many personal patterns related to having a work life that’s DOA, another sacrifice I must make is to let go of control in the establishing of and maintenance of relational connection with others. For the ideas I wish to incubate are nearly all related on one level or another to community building; I like seeing other people pick up the power cords to their own abilities and plug them in. Most of my ideas are related to improving the chances of that happening for individuals by establishing frameworks for community interaction that highlight both needs and opportunities - where the exposures of both of these sides of the coin of life exponentially increases the number of ways in which individuals can exert their own opinions and utilize their usually under-utilized skills, talents and abilities for the common good. I believe we human beings were made to function together like this. So, I am letting myself out of the prison yard of compulsion and death, and moving into the wilds of personal interactions with mindfulness of mutual respect and keeping an open mind, because you never know what you have that someone else needs, or what they have that you might need, or, in the case at hand, that your idea might need. My desire is to meet my goal of furnishing my son and others with full reparations by using my abilities to perceive and conceive, to let people see how amazing God is and what good ideas He has by setting aside all my junk and let HIM birth good stuff out of me. Thank you for asking to answer this, Mr. Deer. I hope it is helpful to some one out there.
Answer_with_writing_sample: To be truly content with my life, I feel that one thing I absolutely need is a deep sense of connection—with myself, my loved ones, and the world around me. This connection is not just a fleeting feeling; it’s an ongoing commitment to understanding and nurturing relationships, as well as recognizing the importance of self-awareness and personal growth. To achieve this, I would sacrifice a lot of the superficial distractions that often cloud our lives, like the incessant scroll through social media or the pressure to conform to societal expectations. I would willingly let go of the chase for material possessions that don’t bring lasting happiness. Instead, my focus would shift towards spending quality time with family and friends, engaging in meaningful conversations, and experiencing shared moments of joy or even vulnerability. It’s about prioritizing those who matter most and investing my time in activities that feed my soul—such as volunteering, pursuing hobbies, or exploring the great outdoors. I have learned that true contentment doesn’t come from things or status but from the depth of the bonds we create and the authenticity we embrace. Therefore, I would gladly sacrifice any fleeting pleasures or superficial accolades to cultivate a life rich in connection, understanding, and genuine fulfillment. In the grand scheme, that’s what truly nourishes my spirit and makes life worthwhile.
Answer_with_user_profile: To be truly content with my life, I believe the one essential thing I need is a genuine sense of connection with others. In a world flooded with digital interactions and superficial conversations, it’s the deep, meaningful relationships that truly nourish the soul. This connection goes beyond friendships; it encompasses family ties, community bonds, and even the empathy we show towards strangers. To cultivate this kind of depth, I would willingly sacrifice the allure of materialism—those fleeting possessions that often distract us from what really matters. I would let go of the constant chase for status or accolades that society deems important. Instead, I would prioritize moments spent with loved ones, heartfelt conversations that last until the early morning, and shared experiences that build lasting memories. I often reflect on how easy it is to get caught up in work or personal ambitions, which can lead to isolation. So, I would sacrifice late nights in the office and the pursuit of perfectionism for evenings spent in laughter and vulnerability with those I care about. By fostering those authentic connections, I find a sense of belonging and fulfillment that no career achievement can replicate. Ultimately, it’s about creating a life rich in love and genuine relationships that brings enduring happiness, which means everything else pales in comparison.
Answer_with_full_information: The one thing I truly feel I need to be content with my life is a deep sense of purpose that resonates with my core values and passions. This purpose could manifest in many forms: meaningful work, a vibrant community, or impactful service to others. To achieve this, I would be willing to sacrifice comfort and familiarity. It might mean stepping out of my current routine and embracing uncertainty, leaning into challenges that push my limits. I would sacrifice leisure time, replacing it with efforts to develop skills that align with this purpose, whether that be through education or hands-on experiences. I would also be prepared to let go of relationships that drain my energy or detract from my goals, understanding that not everyone will share my vision or support my journey. Additionally, I would willingly set aside financial security, recognizing that sometimes investment in one’s dreams may initially lead to instability. However, I believe that the journey of pursuing a purposeful life is worth the sacrifices, as it often brings a profound sense of fulfillment and clarity. At the end of the day, it’s not just about personal gains; it’s about contributing to the greater good and leaving a legacy that inspires others. It’s this commitment to a purpose-driven life, even amidst uncertainties and sacrifices, that I believe will ultimately lead to a rich and satisfying existence.

Question: What happens when I pray for someone else's good?
Old_Answer: It’s funny to me looking at the results about this issue in Wiki, because the VERY limited number of “scientific” studies that have been done on prayer in any systematic way often indicates prayer for someone else does not impact their welfare. Yet, a Christian man named John G. Lake, who in his later years had a ministry in Spokane, Washington, where he was hated by the medical establishment because every time he prayed for people, the hospitals would be emptied. Now, even if we credit the angry doctors with good intentions (“How can you deceive people like this? This is only ‘placebo’ effect and in days their welfare will be worse than ever, and some may even DIE!!!”), we gotta ask, ‘What was really happening?’ It was also John G. Lake, mentioned recently (Mar 17, 2020) in the Times Advocate, who took “plague [that] was very much alive…in his hand and held it under a microscope. The plague bacteria instantly died in Lake's hand.” This isn’t made up, it is true. Thought itself, whether or not it is “prayer” has an energy in it, and therefore, of course, can manifest something. Prayer, if done in concert with a relationship with God, through the ONLY door, the ONLY gate, that there is on Earth, Jesus Christ, has as strong an impact as the combined intensity and purification (holiness) of the prayer warrior is capable of producing. Mother Theresa of Calcutta, India, prayed during the middle of a war conflict in Israel, to ask God to stop the firing of weapons long enough for her to go in and retrieve the wounded; the fighting stopped, she and her workers rushed to the wounded, retrieved the, left the battle sight, and the battle immediately resumed. And, no, there was not a call out from UN troops to let her in. Was it prayer? The Catholics have a term: Divine Union. They, being often intellectually steeped in long and deep studies of history and other matters, sometimes think of the spiritual life in Christ as a process, and that perpetual Divine Union with the Godhead is the desired end. Perhaps this is a good way to think about progress in the spiritual life in Christ. The closer I get to Christ, the more freedom I have to both see and then promptly disavow both my carnal sin and my iniquity which functions in me; then, I can more easily abide in Him, who through me will ONLY express God’s will, which is led and directed by Love, and flow in Truth, Mercy, Justice, Peace… and so on. So, you have an urge to pray?! PRAY ON young master, PRAY ON!
Answer_with_writing_sample: When you pray for someone else's good, you engage in an act that transcends the mere words uttered; it becomes a conduit of positive energy and intent. What I’ve found through my own experiences is that such prayers often create a ripple effect, not just in the life of the person for whom you’re praying, but also within yourself. You see, when you focus on someone else’s well-being, it cultivates a sense of empathy and connection, reinforcing the bond we share as humans. It’s as if you’re fortifying your care and concern through a spiritual medium. Additionally, there’s an interesting psychological component at play—when you invest your mental and emotional resources in wishing well for another, it can enhance your own feelings of gratitude and contentment. This is especially significant in times when we are all facing challenges; shifting our focus outward can alleviate our own burdens and instill a sense of purpose. I’ve often noticed that my prayers seem to invite a wave of hope and strength, both for the person I’m praying for and for myself. And while the outcome may not always be as we envision, there’s a profound reminder that our intentions matter—sometimes in ways we cannot fully comprehend. Ultimately, this practice is not merely about seeking results but about fostering a spirit of love, kindness, and community that can uplift us all. So, whether it's healing, guidance, or support, praying for someone else opens the door for grace to flow, touching lives beyond our immediate awareness

Additionally, engaging in prayer can create a mental and emotional space where hope resides, both for the person in need and for ourselves as the pray-ers. It’s like sending a ripple of positive energy into the universe—what we wish for someone else can ultimately reflect back upon us, enhancing our own outlook and sense of purpose. Even if we don't see immediate results, there is often a sense of peace and fulfillment that accompanies the act of selflessly praying for another. In essence, when we pray for someone else’s good, we’re not just hoping for their upliftment; we’re also engaging in a transformative process that enriches our own lives, creating a cycle of love, hope, and mutual support.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: How does Benny Hinn get people to fall down and act like they do once they are on the ground?
Old_Answer: I thought it was phony. I had a then-older friend who had a mess of a house, a terrible childhood, widowhood from a man whom she might have been surely better off without as he used to beat her and their son, and she LOVED Benny Hinn. She was also a VERY powerful “prayer” warrior. Phenomenal at prophecy, though extremely humble and nearly non-existent ego. When I would stop by or call and hear Benny Hinn in the background, I said nothing, but I would just think, perhaps as you or MANY others do, “Well, if that comforts her, more power to her!” WOW, was I arrogant. I had NO idea this stuff was real. I mean NONE. Makes sense though, doesn’t it? For some of us who jump to conclusions that because our experience hasn’t been a certain way, a certain experience must be manufactured, false, or made up? I think so. Well, after my friend died, my son and I were invited to visit a Friday night meeting with a lady “prophet” who “walked in healing” and so on, (those quotes mean she has the spiritual gift(s) of healing and prophecy). People were going up and “getting slain by the spirit.” I thought, okay, what the heck… when my son asked if he should go up. I said sure, if you want. My son has some very special gifts anyway, and I had learned to trust his judgment on certain things, but I sure as heck didn’t need it. He went up, the lady put her hand on his chest, without any force really, then looked up at him when he didn’t “go down.” She stepped back and thought, or prayed, or both, and then put her hand on him again, with a little more force, and WHOMP, he went down and stayed down. Now, skeptics may feel, or conclude, this is hocus pocus, she pushed him down. Nah, my kid was 6′2″ and 170 pounds then and I can guarantee he wasn’t “pushed” down… But, you say, auto-suggestion… Nah, my son IS gullible in some ways… but NOT in this manner. He takes spiritual stuff seriously. He knows it’s not a game and he doesn’t take anyone else’s word, including his mother’s, for anything. Stubborn “young” fool that he is. Anyway, truly, he sorts it all out himself. Well, he went down and stayed down for a bit; when he came back to the chair next to me, he just felt to me to be a bit more relaxed. Okay, REALLY relaxed. But he didn’t say much to me about it until much much later, a couple YEARS later. We went to visit Charis Bible College here in Colorado Springs, Colorado, one Sunday for a special healing service where they had arranged to bring in a world renown “healer.” He had called on the Wednesday prior to let them know he couldn’t make it…. he was worn out and needed rest, and so he cancelled What were Pastor Lawson Purdue and Andrew Wommack to do? Well, they decided to go ahead and have the event, and they put themselves wholly into the event. My son and I were sitting in the back. There was a long time period after a lesson of sorts, of people of all ages sizes and shapes ministering to those who asked for healing all around the large auditorium off of Elkton (this is before their move up to Woodland Park). A minister of Lawson’s came up to me when I was interceding while others were praying for a woman wheelchair-bound with multiple sclerosis. “Ma’am, Do you need healing?” “Oh, no, I’m fine, I’M PRAYING FOR OTHERS,” I proudly announced, because you see, NO ONE’S GONNA fool around with MY BODY, MY HEALING, MY SPIRITUAL LIFE…. I’m no fool!!!! Oh, but what a fool I was, my intellect pierced through with pride. Fortunately for me, the band of do-gooders around this one woman in the wheelchair dissolved, and all of a sudden, I find myself faced with this Texan in a 10-gallon hat, saying, loudly, “MA’AM, may I pray for your?” And barely before I could get a syllable out, this guy has his hand on my neck, and I start feeling this INCREDIBLE feeling, this warmth, like I have never felt before in my life, or since. AND THEN this thing started happening… It was like a humongous, hot flapping butterfly was on top of my head, flapping his wings up and down, up and down, but I wasn’t letting go. I looked around, I weigh a good deal, and I thought, I am not going down with catchers around me… there seemed to be none; the phenomenon continued, all of a sudden, my son was behind me with another man, THEN I remembered what my son had finally told me one day about his experience with that lady, “I just knew, Mom, that if I let go it would feel really, really, good.” I let go. BAM… I went down into those men’s arms and laid on that floor for a bit. I had never had anything like this happen to me, though I was filled with the Holy Ghost when I had a priest in the Episcopal Church lay his apostolic bishopy hand on my head for confirmation in sixth grade… (I began to speak in tongues afterwards but did not know what that was). But, the most amazing thing about this experience, is that it didn’t end. For TWO WEEKS solid, I was in another world. It was like, and believe, me, I had never ever ever put these silly sounding words together in the same sentence before, and no, no one told me this is what you say, or what not, but it was like a few drops of “golden anointing oil,” had been spread throughout my whole being. It was one of the loveliest experiences I have ever had in my life. So, that’s MY experience. But it wasn’t about Benny Hinn. This one is: Todd White was meeting a drug dealer. Addicted to porn by age 10, drugs by 12, this then teen-ager, had conceived the brilliant plan (a way to get yourself shot, actually) to cheat a drug dealer by pretending he was an undercover cop and demanding on the goods…. When the shots started to ring out from the dealer’s 9mm, White was standing next to his car and only about 10 to 12 feet I think it was from the gun. The bullets did not hit him; It was as though they went THROUGH HIM into other objects around him. He got in his car and sped off in total shock and freaked out then heard a voice, “I took those bullets for you, Todd.” Great, Todd thought, now I’m f***ed with the dealer, gonna get killed, AND I’m losing my mind. But there is was again. And then he told Todd he was Jesus. Which freaked him out ever more. So, without going into more detail, Todd was saved that night, and began growing in the Lord right away, but was not getting the results he wanted. He wanted his laying of hands on people to work, just the way the bible says. He wanted to see the blind see and the deaf hear and lame walk. So, he decided to try some Christian conferences. At one, he decided to sit up front. All of a sudden, the speaker pointed at him and told him to come up front. Todd was surprised, but went up. The man looked at Todd, who was several feet from him, with two very large men behind him to “catch” him or help if anything went down. All of a sudden, the man said something, made a move with his arm toward Todd, and TODD AND THE TWO CATCHERS went up in the air four feet and BACK six feet as they heard what sounded like crackling in the air… something like thunder. Todd was stunned, the catchers were caught off guard. And as Todd came around, and sat up and then stood up, he stood in front of the man once more, and said, “AGAIN.” BOOM, up four feet (with the other two BIG guys, again) and back six. Todd was discombobulated. Could not speak. Was receiving power from on high and did not know his name hardly. Years later, however, my son told me one reason why kids might do that behavior. The young of other mammals, and our little children as well, “know” when mom, their chief protector most of the time, is TIRED. Running off to a safe, sheltered, dark place and hiding can be a defense mechanism that is based in instincts! What an insight! Makes total sense to me now! What does this have to do with your Dad?
